h: A few tips for your walk out to sea
p: Brighton station is about a fifteen-minute walk downhill to the seafront, so you don't need a car to get here, and honestly you're better off without one on a sunny weekend. Head straight down towards the sea and the pier is right in front of you.

How long you spend is up to you. A wander to the end and back with a doughnut can take less than an hour, but add in a few rides, a sit-down meal and some time in the amusements and it's easily a half-day job. Going early in the day, or out of school holidays, makes everything feel a lot more relaxed.

Hang on to your chips. Brighton's gulls are bold, quick and very experienced, and they've snatched many a lunch straight out of an unsuspecting hand. Eat with your back to a wall or under cover and you'll keep more of your dinner.
The pier is lovely in any season, but a breezy winter walk with the sea crashing underneath has a magic of its own. Wrap up, because it can get properly blowy over the water.

For a longer day, Sea Life Brighton is right by the entrance to the pier, and Volk's Electric Railway trundles along the seafront nearby, a fun old-fashioned ride for kids. Look west along the coast and you'll spot the skeleton of the old West Pier standing out in the sea, a slightly haunting reminder of Brighton's other famous pier and a great photo at sunset. The beach itself is pebbly rather than sandy, so pack something comfy to sit on.
